We use this exchange of letters between a professor who wore a #BlackLivesMatter t-shirt to class and one or more anonymous students (they claim they were students) in my @AU_SPA class and project on civil discourse. https://t.co/3UcReJoK2B

5/ 
Conversely, she claims opponents of #BlackLivesMatter can't turn it into an exclusionary or racist term by force of will. That doesn't answer the question what the #MAGAHat means.  Or does it?

6/ 
The prof also says "unless you speak for the Black Lives Matter Movement you have no authority to say what those words mean to the people in it." 

That formulation should satisfy supporters of #BlackLivesMatter (like me) but it leaves them in a pickle re: #MAGAHat

7/ Can we say both that only #BLM advocates know what it means but #MAGAHat wearers decide what that symbol means? One problem: people disagree about what white supremacy and racism means. Most people who study racism see a system baked into US society- not a personal mindset.
